Subject: RE: Planning for 50-GPU baseline and staged activation

Elena —

Appreciate the clear ask and the traffic file. Attached is a compact workbook that lays out three distinct 'rollforward' scenarios (we labelled them A / B / C) that trade off economics, activation cadence, and warmup effort. Short summary here: 

Scenario A — Fast ramp, higher initial commitment
- Baseline: 50 GPU active by week 2 after contract effective date
- Min guarantee month 1: 45 GPUs
- Warmup: ~36–48 hours of continuous warm traffic to reach steady KV cache and batch efficiencies
- Burst approach: Dedicated 4x burst lanes for <15% of peak traffic with price premium; automatic fallback to compatible model family if burst capacity unavailable
- Best if you need immediate throughput and tight latency SLOs

Scenario B — Staggered activation (recommended for engineering validation)
- Baseline: 20 GPUs active week 1, +15 GPUs week 3, +15 GPUs week 6 -> 50 by week 6
- Min guarantee month 1: 20 GPUs
- Warmup: incremental warmup periods after each tranche (12–24 hours each)
- Burst approach: Shared burst pool with soft-priority for Elysium; lower price but higher chance of transient throttling during simultaneous peaks
- Good balance for teams that want gradual model validation and cost smoothing

Scenario C — Conservative start with optional credits
- Baseline: 10 GPUs start, optional purchase of reserved warmup credits that convert to capacity later
- Min guarantee month 1: 10 GPUs
- Warmup: minimal; uses caching strategies to reduce cold-start penalties
- Burst approach: On-demand regional capacity with higher per-token costs and a slightly higher latency profile
- Best if you need lowest near-term commitment while retaining a path to 50 GPUs in 90 days

Attached: elysium_capacity_model_50gpu.xlsx — worksheet pages include weekly activation timeline, expected token/hour coverage per GPU vram profile, estimated first 30d burn rate, and suggested PO language (billing cadence & invoicing).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm which scenario you prefer and we will generate a draft commercial term sheet.
2) Karthik will provide SLO guardrails and a short checklist for model onboarding.
3) If procurement wants a single-line PO, we can produce a minimal PO wording in the workbook.

Happy to jump on a 30-min sync with your procurement team if that helps.

Best —
Sergio Alvarez

Elena / team —

Quick commercial notes to supplement Sergio's scenarios: 

- Pricing anchors: Scenario A is ~18% higher monthly invoice vs Scenario B when normalized to steady-state 50 GPUs due to guaranteed minimums; Scenario C carries higher unit token costs during bursts. Exact numbers are in the "pricing" tab of the workbook.
- SLA/credits: For Scenario A we can offer a 99.9% latency SLO credit ladder; Scenario B gets 99.8% with a conditional escalation pathway (we'll log incidents + auto-fallback to compatible model families).
- Onboarding timeline & dependencies: Egress/VPC peering (2–5 business days), KMS onboarding if you want customer-managed keys (3–7 bd), and model validation windows (we recommend two 24-hour continuous load windows).
- PO language: see sheet "PO_template_short" — includes invoicing cadence options (monthly vs quarterly) and warmup credit mechanics.

I've attached a short pricing summary for your procurement brief. If you confirm Scenario B, I can run a final price check and include a one-time onboarding credit (applied within first invoice).

— Marissa
